newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy slams lack of EU policy cohesion on Iraq.
newsitem.headline: Italy slams lack of EU policy cohesion on Iraq.

text.p: Italy on Monday criticised the failure of European Union countries to agree a common stance on U.S. missile attacks on Iraq and singled out France for pursuing its own agenda.
Foreign Minister Lamberto Dini told parliament that the differing positions had "once again prevented the European Union from exercising a positive influence in a crisis".
He said the inability of the Europeans to speak with one voice on the issue had highlighted the need for a common foreign and security policy in the 15-nation bloc.
"Let us hope that the recent crisis will induce all European governments to reflect seriously," Dini told a joint session of the foreign affairs commissions of both houses of parliament.
European countries differed substantially in their response to U.S. cruise missile strikes on Iraqi air defences last week after Saddam Hussein sent troops into Kurdish territory in northern Iraq.
Britain and Germany voiced staunch support for the American military strikes, and Italy spoke cautiously of its "inevitability" while France was sharply critical.
Dini noted that some Italian politicians had criticised the government for failing to echo France.

"Yes, France did criticise the American decisions for very legitimate reasons but certainly not, as some people in Italy would have us believe, so as to encourage a greater role for the United Nations," Dini said.

"Indeed, it is well known that France is especially keen on its own foreign policy prerogatives, often not hesitating to make its own decisions prevail over the views and intentions of supranational institutions".
Dini had a testy relationship with President Jacques Chirac when he was Italy's prime minister, clashing with him last year over France's nuclear tests in the South Pacific.

Chirac met Dini's successor as prime minister, Romano Prodi, in June when both men said they had agreed to a new era of warm relations. Officials in Paris said on Monday that Chirac and Prodi would meet again on October 3-4 for a bilateral summit.
